Model, geometry, precomputed data & precision

What is calculated

The actual n = 3 SCF surface and saved Nᵣ = 14, Lmax = 8 Galerkin eigenfunctions are used. The primary is at local x = 0, its companion at +x, and the spin is +z. Both stars orbit their barycentre in the inertial view. The companion-facing axes rotate with the binary.

F(t) = F₀(i,φ) + ε Re[D(i,φ) exp(iψ₀ − iωco t)]. The complex response includes temperature, surface area, normals and both moving eclipse boundaries. A pulsating primary can change how much secondary light is blocked.

Geometry & normalization

q = M₂/M₁ = 1; d = 3 R₁D; R₁D = 1 R☉; each mass is 1.00594 M☉. P = — day. Inclination is measured from +z. In the corotating frame α(t) = −2πt/P, with α = 0 at the primary eclipse. The same observer is fixed in the inertial frame.

Fluxes use a constant mean equilibrium, uneclipsed binary reference at each inclination. The initial mode phase and amplitude are adjustable; the secondary has no intrinsic oscillation. The colour scale is normalized per mode to expose its spatial pattern.

Cached forward calculations

Loading cached integration details.

Periodic interpolation is applied to the equilibrium flux and the real and imaginary response, followed by the exact mode phase at elapsed time. Inclination snapping selects an actual cached geometry; turn it off to interpolate between inclinations. Changing the inspection camera does not change any flux.

The precision report is included with the offline download.

Physical approximations

The symmetric secondary uses the same n = 3 shape. The inherited SCF calculation treated its companion as a point mass; this is not a new two-fluid equilibrium. Radiation is bolometric Planck intensity with flux-normalized linear limb darkening u = 0.4, T ∝ g0.25.

τ = −(2/3)∇·ξ at ζ = 0.995 is an adiabatic temperature proxy, not a nonadiabatic photospheric solution. The light curve is linear in mode amplitude. Irradiation, beaming and light-travel time are excluded. Surface refinement and geometry interpolation affect numerical precision; this is a research exploration tool.
